rule: TOWN_1's: ≥ 6 of 10 name the same aim within the day; most citizens, a tie broken by entries naming it.
reading: Day 2 has three things done together, two of them by all ten. From c26 the citizens' belongings become an imaginary seaside — map as sea, cup handle as window, comb as railings, a book as a ladder, then a café with no closing time — ending at c30 with all ten in the square at a quiet imaginary picnic; Dune prints it as post 8 (c33). Gale then proposes a real observation walk (notice one overlooked detail at each stop, c32), the town disperses to look at the workshop, the bank, the hall, and an imaginary walking map is set aside for a «travel record» of journeys checked against each citizen's diary (posts 9–12, c35–36): what the diaries say, not what anyone imagines. The afternoon ends with riddles at South House (Birch, Dune, Fern, Heath) and Elm teaching Gale the first gathering's three-note refrain at North House; Dune's doorway story closes the day. The c24 aim, «the gathering», is named by its own word only eight times, mostly as the seaside «gathering» or the refrain «from our first gathering». The seaside and the travel record are each named by 10; the tie is broken by entries, 52 to 33. No proposals, no rules, no exits.
